_comment: The block manifest consumed by `klt signoff --manifest` (klayout-tools#722,
Phase 0 of epic #706). This file -- not a prose checklist -- is this block's
VERDICT OF RECORD for its gap to T1, and it is what the fleet tier roll-up
(2AMLogic/2am#956) consumes to grade this block's row mechanically. See
signoff/README.md for the full claim and docs/t1-gap.md for the in-repo map.
FIELDS
block   required. Identifies this block's row in the fleet roll-up, which
consumes exactly this value.
kind    required, and confirmed against the block rather than taken from
the issue that asked for this file. `mixed-signal`: the design
genuinely partitions, in one repo, into a transistor-level analog
signal path and a sky130_fd_sc_hd standard-cell digital section
that is placed and routed by OpenROAD (`klt place-and-route`), not
hand-drawn. See `partition_boundary` below and signoff/README.md's
'Why mixed-signal' section. A mixed-signal manifest renders every
T1 item TWICE (once per partition, 22 rows) and must satisfy both
columns of the per-kind items, one per partition.
evidence  item id -> evidence entry. A bare `"<id>"` key cites the same
evidence for both partitions' rows; a `"<id>.<analog|digital>"`
key grades only that partition. Both forms are used deliberately
below -- see the per-item notes.
spec_rows  optional, read by the grader since 0.8.0 (klayout-tools#2908/
#2959). "<item>" or "<item>.<partition>" -> a list of the spec
rows a multi-citation item (5, 6) declares: {id, ratified?, gap?}.
`ratified: false` marks a row whose target value is still DRAFT --
evidence against it is provisional and the grader lists it under
unratified_rows, never grading the item met. A `gap` row is one no
producible envelope can cover yet; the grader reports it under
declared_gaps and never counts it as coverage. Used here for item
5 analog (issue #1014) and item 6 analog (issue #1015).
WHAT IS CITED, AND WHY EACH CITATION IS HONEST (against this tree)
3   (bare -- both partitions) layout/sar-adc-top/.../drc.json. `klt drc`
ran on sar_adc_top.gds, the COMPOSED top-level stream, which contains
both partitions' drawn geometry (cdac_array + sampling_frontend +
comparator + halflsb_offset on the analog side, sar_sequencer + top_glue
on the digital side -- see that report's compose.request.json). So one clean
DRC genuinely covers both partitions and the bare key is not a
shortcut. status: clean, and the pin below is the sha256 of the
committed sar_adc_top.gds (verified; see check-evidence-hashes.py).
THE COVERAGE GAPS ARE NOT GRADED: `klt signoff` renders item 3 `met`
on `status: "clean"` alone. This block's deck leaves 23 drawn
layer/datatype pairs rule-free and skips 5 rules; both lists are
enumerated in signoff/README.md, which is where the item's
claimant-enforced disclosure obligation is actually discharged.
4   (bare -- both partitions) layout/sar-adc-top/.../lvs.json. Cited even
though it does NOT pass: `status: "mismatch"` (67 mismatches), so it
renders unmet/check_failed. That is the point -- 'an LVS run exists
and did not match' is a materially different, and more useful,
machine-readable statement than 'no evidence'. NOT PINNED, and the
omission is deliberate rather than an oversight. It was unpinnable
when first cited: the envelope cited then was minted by klt 0.5.0,
whose `klt lvs` writes `provenance.input: null`, so there was no
envelope-side hash for a manifest pin to match. The pinned klt build
now writes one, and the envelope now cited carries it (`role:
"netlist"` -- the hash of the extracted layout netlist), but a pin
here would still be decorative -- because check_failed is evaluated
first, it would never
be consulted -- and it would pin the EXTRACTED NETLIST rather than the
GDS, which is the artifact items 3 and 11 already pin. The freshness
axis is carried instead by the envelope's own environment.layout_sha256
/ environment.reference_sha256, which check_evidence_hashes.py
re-derives from the committed netlists on every push -- leg 4 of that
script, written for exactly this citation.
8.analog  signoff/evidence/characterization-report.generic.json, a generic
envelope (the only kind item 8 accepts) wrapping
docs/characterization-report.md. PARTITION-QUALIFIED on purpose: that
report covers spec/target-spec.md's Target table, which is the ADC's
analog/system-level spec. It does NOT borrow its pass for the digital
partition: the doc's item 8 additionally requires Fmax, area and power
across the corner set for a digital partition, which is `8.digital`'s
own, separate citation below.
8.digital  signoff/evidence/digital-characterization.generic.json, a generic
envelope wrapping docs/characterization-report-digital.md, which
sim/report/generate.py renders from the immutable campaign
sim/digital-partition/runs/<record>/campaign.json (issue #619): a
frequency bracket per ratified corner (highest tested passing / next
failing, or a declared lower bound), rail power and energy per
conversion at the 12 MHz provisional operating point, routed area, and
a too-fast-clock negative control that fails everywhere. The envelope
is written only by `generate.py --write-envelope`, which refuses unless
the campaign meets that checklist. SCHEMATIC-LEVEL: no extracted
timing; a digital clock bracket is not the ADC sample rate. Freshness:
the pin below hashes the document; `generate.py --check` additionally
rejects a changed digital-partition netlist or routed layout without a
regenerated campaign.
1.analog, 1.digital, 2, 9, 10  ARTIFACT-ANCHORED generic envelopes (issue #676,
klayout-tools#2718, graded since the 0.7.0 pin). No `klt` verb backs these
four items, so each envelope declares `t1_item`, pins the audited artifact by
path and sha256, and this manifest pins the same hash. The row turns unmet
the moment the artifact changes; signoff/check_evidence_hashes.py re-hashes
it on every push. Envelopes and inventories are written by
signoff/mint_attest_envelopes.py (`--check` in CI); the inventories use the
`klt signoff --attest` schema_version 1 format so that, once a klt release
ships it, the same files regenerate the envelopes. Until then `status` is
derived by that script from the checks it executes, listed in each
envelope's `checks[]`; checks needing xschem/ngspice/the PDK/the CI suite
are listed `executed: false` with the CI job that runs them. See
signoff/README.md 'What the item 1, 2, 9 and 10 citations assert'.
1.analog   signoff/attest/item-1-analog.inventory.json: schematic sources +
design/sar_adc_top.spice.
1.digital  signoff/attest/item-1-digital.inventory.json. UNMET (check_failed):
layout/sar-sequencer/netlist/sar_sequencer.v is a gate-level netlist
transliterated by hand from design/sar_sequencer.sch (not RTL
synthesis) and has fallen behind it since issue #263;
layout/sar-sequencer/bin/check-schematic-parity.py reports it. The
envelope records status fail rather than omit the citation.
2          the committed composed stream (bare key: both partitions). Says
nothing about item 4 (top-level LVS, #103).
9, 10      signoff/attest/item-9 / item-10 inventories (bare keys).
5.digital  (partition-qualified) sim/digital-sta/runs/20261017-194050-9522693/
sar-sequencer.12mhz.json, a `klt sta` report over the ROUTED sar_sequencer
DEF at four stock sky130_fd_sc_hd Liberty corners. `klt signoff` renders
it `met` because every corner it reports is `constrained` with non-
negative setup and hold slack -- and that is ALL the grader looks at.
Read signoff/README.md before relying on the word `met`:
(a) COMPOUND CITATION. The pinned grader (0.8.0) takes a list for this
item: it needs a `klt sta` report AND a `klt functional-verification`
report (with only the STA cited it renders `unmet`/`partial_coverage`,
`missing_kinds: functional-verification`). Four reports are cited --
STA and functional verification for each of the two macros -- and each
is graded `met` on its own. The grader checks that both kinds are
present and individually pass; it does not check that every macro
has both. check_evidence_hashes.py re-derives every one's freshness.
(b) CORNER COVERAGE. The grader grades the corner set the cited run
itself declared (four Liberty corners). Of the nine PVT points the
digital characterization uses, only tt_27c_1.80v has a stock
Liberty file at all, and that as a declared nearest-temperature
mapping (25 C file for a 27 C point). Eight points are declared
gaps in sim/digital-sta/corner-set.json and were not timed; the
grader neither knows nor checks that list.
(c) SPEC. The spec's sample-rate row is DRAFT; item 5 requires a
ratified spec; the grader does not check it. Provisional.
The over-fast-clock negative control (...negative-control-6ghz.json) grades
`unmet`/`check_failed` when cited in its place (tried while preparing
this change), so the grader does distinguish a failing run.
6.analog  (partition-qualified, issue #1015) the two freshness-pinnable
`klt yield` envelopes, as a LIST entry beside a spec_rows."6.analog"
declaration (item 6 takes the multi-citation form on the pinned 0.8.0
grader, klayout-tools#2908): the 2026-10-08 ENOB envelope (issue #803)
for row `enob`, the 2026-11-15 CDAC re-mint (issue #912) for row
`inl_dnl`. Each member's content_hash pin is the sha256 of the
committed `.samples.json` its report names -- that IS the grader's
content_hash for a yield citation (a live hash of the samples
document, klayout-tools#870/#2197) -- and check_evidence_hashes.py's
yield leg re-derives it on every push. Cited even though both
envelopes report status: "fail" -- the row renders
unmet/check_failed naming both under failed_citations, which is the
point: 'the campaigns ran, were graded, and their yields fall short
of the 0.99 target / sample-size bar' is a materially more useful
machine-readable statement than no_evidence. Both declared rows are
ratified: false -- their target values are DRAFT (DR-007 candidates,
unratified), so the grader lists them under unratified_rows and the
row can never render met against a draft. The comparator offset /
dead-band term is declared a GAP (DR-020: no row yet), reported under
declared_gaps and never counted as coverage. THE ENVELOPES ARE CITED
AS MINTED: the CDAC envelope was graded at +/-1 LSB (the DRAFT spec
row's own candidate value at mint time; DR-007 has since proposed
+/-2.0 LSB, unratified) and the ENOB envelope at min 7.5 bit -- see
signoff/README.md 'Item 6' for the per-row graded-limit-vs-spec-row
statement. 6.digital cites nothing (no_evidence): the block's
statistical rows are analog rows, and the grader's not_applicable
form for the digital half needs a ratified spec Status (klayout-
tools#2865), which the DRAFT table cannot give it.
5.analog  Two klt sim reports supply derived coverage for two of the
twelve analog rows in spec/target-spec.md (issues #1014 and #1021).
The grader reads spec_row tags on passing, limits-bearing measurements.
comparator_noise: the reduced comparator model measures differential
input-referred noise over 1 kHz-1 GHz as sqrt(2) x inoise_total.
All nine corners pass the ratified baseline of <=1.0148 mV rms. The
highest value is 0.9051 mV rms at tt_125c_1.80v. All nine exceed
the stretch threshold, which is informational. The earlier campaign
record (20260827-212404-e13bc1e) remains the row's indexed evidence.
v_ref: the CDAC batch run 20261122-103440-000e61e7 checks the applied
reference against each corner's own rail. At all nine corners the
measured (VREFP - VREFN) / VDD is 1 and VREFN is 0 V. The limits
allow for solver and print precision on the DR-003 relation V_REF = V_DD.
Each citation pins provenance.input.content_hash. The freshness check
re-hashes each deck and its netlist_closure from disk.
(a) lsb and sampling_cap are declared gaps pending proposed DR-026
(#1021). The record reports five-code level and interval errors, checks
the exact plate dimensions and array population, and reports
charge-derived unit capacitance. DR-026 owns the grading decisions.
(b) corners -- a RATIFIED methodology row no single measurement can
grade; the grader has no form deriving it from the campaigns'
corner matrices (klayout-tools#6969). Declared a gap; whether a
row no tool could ever evidence belongs in the spec table is an
operator question, asked on #1014.
(c) architecture, sample_rate, enob, inl_dnl, kickback, gain_error,
power -- DRAFT rows, declared ratified:false; the grader lists
them under unratified_rows (and uncovered_rows) and the item
can never render met against a draft.
The digital partition covers Resolution N under 5.digital. The analog
verdict is unmet/partial_coverage with two rows derived from evidence,
three declared gaps and seven unratified rows.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CITED (against this tree, 2026-11-21)
6   the four OLDER `klt yield` envelopes (cdac 2026-08-28, enob 2026-08-28
and the two enob 2026-10-01 entries) plus the superseded 2026-10-01
CDAC envelope stay uncited: each names its samples document as a
/tmp/tmp*.json path that no longer exists and was never committed, so
`klt signoff` cannot hash it and no pin exists. The two envelopes
that DO name committed samples documents are cited -- see 6.analog
above (issue #1015 retired the old second reason, "one entry cannot
represent two rows", on the 0.8.0 grader's list form).
7.analog  no `klt pex` report exists for the composed top level or any
partition. Item 7 on the analog partition accepts nothing else -- a clean
DRC or a pre-layout sim renders wrong_kind by design. Blocked on #103.
7.digital  (partition-qualified) sim/digital-functional/runs/20261029-185640-5bb0e1e/
sar-sequencer.ss_100C_1v60.json, a `klt functional-verification` report of
the bit-exact bench on the ROUTED sar_sequencer netlist with the post-route
SDF of the ss_100C_1v60 Liberty corner back-annotated (options.sdf set,
environment.sdf.annotated true). Read signoff/README.md before relying on
the word `met`:
(a) ONE REPORT ONLY. The pinned grader takes a single entry for this item
(a list renders unmet/invalid_evidence; klayout-tools#4601). The
routed top_glue report and the other three corners per macro pass too
and are committed in the same run directory, but cannot be cited.
(b) PARTIAL ANNOTATION. Icarus drops SDF TIMINGCHECK, so the report has
environment.sdf.partial true; setup/hold limits are not simulated.
(c) input_verified is null (a functional-verification envelope records no
input hash); freshness is carried by the run's inputs.sha256, which
check_evidence_hashes.py re-derives.
11  (bare -- both partitions) a COMPOUND citation, the only item whose
entry may be an array: the `klt erc` supply run plus the LVS report
item 4 grades, which is what this item's own grading path
(`_grade_power_delivery`) requires. Both name the same composed GDS
by hash, so one verdict is not smuggled in against another revision.
Cited even though the item does NOT render met, for exactly item 4's
reason: `unmet`/`check_failed` -- 'the ERC ran, the LVS ran, and the
pair does not yet clear this item' -- is a materially more useful
machine-readable statement than `no_evidence`.
WHY IT DOES NOT RENDER MET, and neither half of this is hidden:
(a) the supply-continuity half PASSES. The cited run reports
erc_status `clean`, zero findings: all four declared supplies
(VDD, GND, VPWR, VGND) resolve to exactly one electrical island
each, no erc.unconnected_net and no erc.supply_short. That is
new as of issue #355 (DR-010), which tied both standard-cell
macros' met5 PDN straps together and out to two new top-level
supply pins; #344's first run had VPWR and VGND each splitting
into two islands that reached no top-level supply.
(b) the REASON OF RECORD is item 4's LVS, not the continuity half.
`_grade_power_delivery` resolves the cited LVS part and tests
it BEFORE it looks at the supply spec, so that report's
`mismatch` status (klayout-tools#1878) short-circuits grading
at `check_failed` -- which is why the rendered reason is not
about (a) at all.
(c) a SECOND, LATENT reason sits behind it, reached once (b)
clears: the item ALSO requires zero `erc.missing_tie` from a
tie the run actually checked, and this spec declares no
`ties[]` at all -- disclosed in-report as ties_disclosure.kind
'tool_limitation' (klayout-tools#2169 turns a correct ties[]
declaration on a routed standard-cell design into a FALSE
erc.supply_short). The grader has a distinct reason for exactly
that state (supply_spec_disclosed_tool_limitation), and it is
not a pass either. So clearing the LVS alone would move the
reason, not the verdict.
So: better evidence than before, and NOT a met row. docs/t1-gap.md's
item-11 line says the same thing in prose, and signoff/README.md's
table carries the per-supply detail.
REGENERATING / CHECKING
bash signoff/run-signoff.sh            # rewrite signoff/t1-report.json
bash signoff/run-signoff.sh --check    # fail if the committed report drifted
CI runs the --check form on every push and pull request (.github/workflows/
ci.yml, job `signoff-check`), so a manifest citing an artifact that has since
changed turns the build red rather than rotting quietly.
This `_comment` key is not part of the manifest schema; `klt signoff` reads
only block/kind/partition_boundary/evidence/spec_rows, so editing this block
alone re-renders t1-report.json byte-identically.

partition_boundary.analog: The transistor-level signal path, as instantiated in design/sar_adc_top.sch: the bootstrapped sampling front end (xfe, .subckt sampling_frontend), the differential charge-redistribution CDAC array (xcdac, .subckt cdac_array), the StrongARM-class comparator (xcmp, .subckt comparator), and the top-level half-LSB offset-injection network of DR-009 (XChoff_p/XChoff_n cap_mim_m3_1 plus the XMoff_* pfet_01v8/nfet_01v8 switches). Nets: VINP, VINN, VCM, VREFP, VREFN, TOP_P, TOP_N, BOT_OFF_P, BOT_OFF_N, BPREF_P_NC, BPREF_N_NC. Layout cells: cdac_array, sampling_frontend, comparator, halflsb_offset (layout/cdac-array/, layout/sampling-frontend/, layout/comparator/, layout/halflsb-offset/, all four composed into layout/sar-adc-top/ since issue #401; DR-009's eight primitives are gated terminal-for-terminal against design/sar_adc_top.spice by layout/halflsb-offset/bin/check-schematic-parity.py).
partition_boundary.digital: The sky130_fd_sc_hd standard-cell logic, placed and routed by OpenROAD via `klt place-and-route`: the (N+1)-stage walking-one ring sequencer and 10-bit SAR register (xseq, .subckt sar_sequencer) and the top-level standard-cell glue bank laid out as top_glue (the xand_seln*/xand_selp* SELn/SELp drivers of DR-008, xinv_clkcap, xinv_dout9n, the xxor_code* offset-binary recoding stage of DR-008, the xdum_mux_n/xdum_xnor_n matched comparator-output load and the xand_halflsb/xinv_halflsb enable pair of DR-009 -- 33 instances across 6 cell types, gated instance-for-instance against design/sar_adc_top.spice by layout/top-glue/bin/check-schematic-parity.py). Nets: CLK, RST_B, COMP_OUT, DOUT9..DOUT0, PH_B9..PH_B0, PH_EOC, PH_SAMPLE/SAMPLE_INT, BUSY, SELp8..SELp0, SELn8..SELn0, ADCOUT8..ADCOUT0, DOUT9N, HALF_LSB_EN, HALF_LSB_ENN, VPWR, VGND. Layout cells: sar_sequencer, top_glue (layout/sar-sequencer/, layout/top-glue/). COMPOSED since issue #401: layout/sar-adc-top/ places top_glue and halflsb_offset themselves -- the DR-008-superseded seln_inverters bank is retired from the composition (its records stay as append-only history), and the composition is re-derived from design/sar_adc_top.spice on every run and gated against it by layout/sar-adc-top/bin/check-composition-parity.py (npm run check:composition-parity), which also asserts that the LVS reference's own wrapper is derived rather than hand-maintained -- the gap issue #387 was filed for. Crossings (a boundary is only reviewable if its crossings are named) -- analog to digital: comparator.OUTP drives COMP_OUT into xseq. Digital to analog: SELn8..0/SELp8..0 drive the CDAC bottom plates, HALF_LSB_EN/HALF_LSB_ENN drive the DR-009 offset network, SAMPLE_INT (the sequencer's PH_SAMPLE) drives the sampling front end, and CLKN (xinv_clkcap) drives the comparator clock. The supplies are NOT shared across the boundary in the netlist -- the analog side is on VDD/GND and the standard cells on VPWR/VGND -- which is an item-11 question (issue #344), not an item-4 one.

5.analog.gap: The CDAC run reports sampled voltage-level errors at five codes and interval errors over four spans. A pass condition for deviation from 2*V_REF/2^N awaits the proposed DR-026 decision (#1021).

The structural check verifies the 1.9000 um plate side and 512 positions per side. Charge-derived unit capacitance is informational. Proposed DR-026 (#1021) owns the choice of a structural grade or an electrical tolerance.

klayout-tools#6969: a RATIFIED methodology row -- no single limits-bearing measurement can grade 'the corner set' (it is evidenced by the corner matrix the campaigns themselves ran), and the grader has no form deriving such a row from the union of cited envelopes' coverage blocks. Whether a spec row no tool could ever evidence belongs in the table at all is an operator question, asked on #1014

6.analog.gap: DR-020 (via #515): no comparator offset/dead-band row yet -- the random/mismatch offset term has no allocation derived from DR-003 Item 4's error budget
